newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania raises one-week rate to 57 pct from 53 pct.
newsitem.headline: Romania raises one-week rate to 57 pct from 53 pct.

text.p: Romania's central bank said on Thursday it raised the minimum permitted rate for its one-week refinancing funds by four percentage points to 57 percent.

The latest rate rise follows a hike in the central bank's discount rate to 50 percent from 35 percent. The move, in line with International Monetary Fund (IMF) recommendations, was aimed at calming rising inflation.
Year-on-year inflation rose to 47.4 percent last November from October's 45.1 percent, sharply exceeding the 20-percent target agreed with the IMF for 1996.
Inflation is expected to edge up after Romania's new centrist government doubled fuel prices starting in January to match world levels and meet IMF suggestions.
The IMF suspended a three-year standby credit of $460 million after criticising the lax policies of the leftist government that was toppled in last November's general election.
The central bank cut the amount of refinancing funds available at Thursday's auction to 2.15 trillion lei from 2.315 trillion in the previous session last year.
Short-term interbank money market prices, now around 56 percent, and bank deposit rates are expected to rise in line with the tighter monetary policy.

An IMF mission is expected to arrive in Bucharest this month to discuss a new loan accord with the new cabinet, headed by Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea. -- Mirela Eremia, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
